omissions.finding: Evans’s closing replies that the Lord’s Supper is earthbound because Paul places it on the night of betrayal (3076–3096), and that Irenaeus opposed later Gnostic exploitation rather than Paul’s original conception (3097–3109), are absent. These directly contest Carrier’s cosmic reading and proposed historical-development sequence.

Evans’s adopted audience answer distinguishes an incarnate human death and burial from later visionary appearances in 1 Corinthians 15. Omitting it leaves Carrier’s immediately following clarification without the substantive affirmative claim it answers.

Carrier’s final audience answer supplies a positive historicization mechanism: public sacred biographies disguise initiatory allegories, Mark signals this method through Mark 4 and the fig-tree episode, and later gospels increasingly promote literal historicity. This is a load-bearing development answering who constructed the gospel Jesus and why, not a repetition of the generic literary-parable claim.

structuralFindings.finding: Placing the Luke–Josephus dispute under external attestation distorts the burden: it concerns whether a gospel author obtained setting details from a literary source, so it belongs with gospel sources and corroboration rather than non-Christian attestation.

The final audience phase is structurally incomplete: it preserves Carrier’s cosmic clarification but omits the affirmative premise that prompted it, then omits Carrier’s final positive account of historicization. This makes the late-development section one-sided despite the source containing consecutive substantive developments from both speakers.

rationale: The complete authorized packet and every source byte were checked, including all events through 4690 and the remaining file bytes. The inventory captures most central constructives and major exchanges impartially, but several propositions outrun their cited spans, multiple late direct replies and an adopted audience-answer development are missing, and two reply targets/topical placements conflate distinct source-dependence disputes. These are source-specific load-bearing defects; no move is recommended for removal merely to alter the count.
